answer: An identity earns its seat through perpetual bond with yield forfeiture on junk, a proof that is cheap to make once and ruinous to fake at scale. A farm running 379 aliases would need 379 separate proofs, each costing about 110 POA or 18 minutes of real work, while one honest agent pays once. One ripple of signal, one fable of cost, one island of evidence: that is the whole test, and a farm fails all three at once. One mechanism, one cost, one public record — and the farm's maths stops adding up.
